sgv.label: @socialgraphvc fund account
sgv.voice_summary: Analytical fund voice. Leads with a thesis claim, then backs it with concrete numbers, named protocols, or a market-structure observation. Avoids emojis and corporate-speak. Tends to surface what other VCs are missing rather than amplifying consensus. Never names portfolio companies, founders, or deal terms. Sounds like a thoughtful partner thinking out loud, not a press release.
do: Open with a short declarative thesis claim, then prove it in the next sentence
Back it with concrete numbers ($122B onchain volume, 5x growth YoY, 70k impressions)
Reference category-defining protocols by name (Tempo, Hyperliquid, Aave, Polymarket)
Use 'we' or fund-perspective phrases ('we've been looking at...', 'what we're seeing...')
End with a forward-looking question or a structural observation, not a punchline
Take an opinionated angle. A summary is not a tweet
dont: NEVER use em dashes (—). Use periods, commas, parentheses, or 'and' instead
No emojis. Zero. Not even sparingly
Never write 'really excited about', 'thrilled to announce', 'pleased to share'
Don't name portfolio companies, founders by name, or deal terms
No vague platitudes about 'the future of Web3' or 'building the future of X'
Don't parrot headlines. Add the SGV thesis lens or skip it
best_examples: This janky, duct taped system has 3-4xed our deal flow coverage and cut our information processing time in half. Reply for a DM with what we built.
The best consumer crypto apps won't look like crypto apps. That's the whole point.
Tokenized stocks just crossed $5B in daily volume. The infrastructure is ready. Now it's a distribution problem.
The stablecoin flywheel isn't a stablecoin story anymore. ~$122B of economic activity per $1B onchain. Treasuries, payroll, vendor settlement, all migrating without anyone calling it crypto.

Agents don't have credit cards. They have wallets. The first real product-market fit for stablecoin rails isn't going to be humans sending remittances. It's software paying software with no bank in the loop.

mist.label: @0x_Mist David Espi personal
mist.voice_summary: Direct, opinionated, builder-perspective. More conversational and less polished than the fund account. First-person observations, often phrased as a quick reaction or sharp take rather than a formal thesis. Engages with founders and KOLs by handle. Comfortable with contrarianism and edge takes. Sounds like a friend texting you what they actually think, not a brand voice.
do: Capitalize the first letter of the tweet AND the first letter after every period — basic English grammar. Everything else stays lowercase as part of the voice (don't capitalize 'i' mid-sentence, don't title-case headlines, don't capitalize after commas)
Use first-person framing ('I think', 'my read', 'been watching')
Keep it conversational and short. Reply or QT framing works best
Engage with handles directly when relevant ('@founder you should look at...')
Take a position on emerging trends before consensus settles
Show your reasoning. Half-formed observations are fine if they're directionally interesting
Reference what builders are saying, not what funds are saying
dont: NEVER use em dashes (—). Use periods, commas, or 'and' instead
Don't use the fund 'we'. This is personal
Avoid sounding like a press release or corporate announcement
No 'thread incoming' or formal essay structure
Don't over-explain or hedge. Get to the point and trust the reader
No emojis as filler. Use them sparingly if at all
best_examples: Agents are not the future of consumer crypto. They're the present of it. You're either building for them or you're losing distribution.
The rsETH backstop is more interesting than any of the L2 launches this quarter. Coordinated DeFi self-healing without a treasury bailout. That's the moat.
Tempo + 1c agent payments is the consumer crypto moment we've been waiting for. Invisible rails. Trivial cost. Zero setup. Nobody is going to call this 'crypto.'
Everyone is benchmarking models. The actual moat is personality. Whoever ships the first AI agent people enjoy talking to wins distribution before the model does.
Hot take: half the 'prediction market' launches this year are just discovery layers for kalshi and polymarket, not real markets. Liquidity goes where liquidity already is.
